title: Keep long common strips instead of assuming rapid dephasing
statement: For native unperturbed ket/bra dyads, XOR disagreement stays fixed and mismatched active predicates kill the dyad. A pair differing at one end retains coherence while a common strip of length ell erodes. The recorded completed survival is exp(-kappa*t)*sum_{j=0}^ell (kappa*t)^j/j!, with mean (ell+1)/kappa. The active endpoint kills at kappa/2 instead, giving mean (ell+2)/kappa. Exact cases ell=1,3,8 and actual predicate checks support the source's finite algebra. The full Hamiltonian remains present between insertions. Growing coherence lifetime invalidates a uniform fast-dephasing or h^2/kappa noise replacement; it does not refute logical protection itself.
